mentions.author: Someone
mentions.text:
I don’t think they archived their benchmarks. Even then, I think that would be a multi-month project, to verify whether the test cases still are representative of real-world usage.

A factor of 2 would IMO be worth it, though.

Cursory reading [link], I get the impression FreeBSD switches over to a ¿bubble sort? (I didn’t look close) at <7 elements.

That function also seems newer (it claims to implement [course], which is from 1993)

mentions.author: hyperpape
mentions.story: “Use bubble sort for insertion sets, because it's faster than std::stable_sort”
mentions.text:
This touches on an interesting topic: how robust implementations of most algorithms go well beyond what you're taught in an algorithms course. There are tons of optimizations that matter when dealing with real world data that don't matter for algorithmic complexity.

Two links on the subject:

Bentley and McIlroy on Engineering a Sort Function: [course]

Tim Peters' Timsort: [link]
